This page walks through everything you need installed before the first class. Most
of our code is in **Python**, and we'll write both `.py` scripts and Quarto `.qmd`
reports. **We do not use Jupyter notebooks (`.ipynb`) in this course.**

::: {.callout-note}
Some setup steps below are still being written. Check back before the semester
starts.
:::

## What we'll use

| Purpose | Tool |
|---|---|
| Terminal and code editor | A terminal plus [VS Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/) or [Positron](https://positron.posit.co/) |
| Version control | [Git](https://git-scm.com/) and a [GitHub](https://github.com/) account |
| Python environments | [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) |
| Linting and testing | [ruff](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/) and [pytest](https://docs.pytest.org/) |
| Data | [polars](https://pola.rs/), [plotnine](https://plotnine.org/), [Great Tables](https://posit-dev.github.io/great-tables/) |
| LLMs from Python | [chatlas](https://posit-dev.github.io/chatlas/) |
| MCP servers | the [MCP Python SDK](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk) (FastMCP) |
| Reports | [Quarto](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/) |
| An AI coding agent | [Claude Code](https://www.claude.com/product/claude-code) or [Codex](https://github.com/openai/codex) |

## Quarto and Python

Quarto renders `.qmd` files containing Python code using its Jupyter engine. You
won't ever open or create a notebook, but the project's uv environment needs
`ipykernel` installed, and Quarto has to use that environment. The simplest way is
to run Quarto through uv:

```bash
uv add ipykernel
uv run quarto render report.qmd
```

## Choose and install an AI coding agent

We will use agentic coding tools all semester, so you need one. Instruction will use
**Claude Code** and **Codex**, and the underlying skills transfer between them.

### Step 1: Get a subscription (about $20/month)

- Claude Code requires at least a [Claude Pro](https://claude.ai/login?plan=pro)
  subscription. A free account isn't enough.
- Codex requires a paid [ChatGPT plan](https://chatgpt.com/pricing) (Plus is fine).

We recommend a **subscription rather than API billing** because agentic coding uses
so many tokens that per-token API costs would be far higher. Check Slack for whether
the class has an institutional arrangement before paying for your own.

### Step 2: Install your agent

Follow the official instructions: the
[Claude Code quickstart](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/quickstart) or the
[Codex repository](https://github.com/openai/codex). If you get stuck, we'll sort it
out together before or after the first class.

### Other agents

You're welcome to use another agent (Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot, OpenCode...).
In-class instruction will use Claude Code and Codex, so you may need to translate
tool-specific steps yourself.

### Claude Code ↔ Codex

Both tools read the same open standards, so most of what we build works in either:

| Concept | Claude Code | Codex |
|---|---|---|
| Project instructions | `CLAUDE.md` (we'll have it import `AGENTS.md`) | `AGENTS.md` |
| Skills (`SKILL.md`) | `.claude/skills/` | `.agents/skills/` |
| MCP servers | supported | supported |

Features like plan mode, hooks, and subagents differ between the two tools. We'll
note the differences as we reach each topic.

## API access for chatlas (Meetings 10–11)

A Claude or ChatGPT subscription does **not** include API access. For the
chatlas meetings you have three options, and the code is the same for all of them
(you change one line to switch providers):

1. **Free:** the Gemini API free tier (via chatlas's `ChatGoogle`).
2. **Free:** a local model through [Ollama](https://ollama.com/) (via `ChatOllama`).
3. **About $5:** load credit with a provider and use a small, cheap model.

We'll cover how to set this up, and how to keep API keys out of your code and out of
your Git history, in class before Meeting 10.
